title: Planner integrity follow-up: parent linking + global sequence allocation
summary: Fix the remaining planner integrity bugs surfaced by F010/P037 creation: unresolved human refs in write paths and duplicate global sequence allocation under concurrent task creation.
description:
Follow-up phase to P035(F005) after a new real regression/integrity incident observed during creation of F010/P037.

Observed failures in the live planner state:
- `F010` exists but currently reports `0 phases`.
- `P037` exists with 11 tasks (`T142..T152`) but is not listed under `F010`.
- During the first creation attempt, parallel task creation produced duplicate `T141` identifiers before the phase was deleted and recreated serially.

Why this phase exists:
- P035 fixed a class of bugs where planner write commands accepted human refs like `F005` / `P034` / `T140` but did not always resolve them before mutation.
- The new incident suggests either a remaining uncovered path/regression in feature↔phase linking or a repair/render path that still tolerates unresolved parents.
- The duplicate `T141` event is a separate integrity issue in global sequence allocation/counter updates and must be fixed at the data layer, not merely avoided operationally.

Code areas to inspect first:
- `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts` for feature/phase/task persistence, counters, and repair logic.
- `packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts` plus any naming/sequence helpers in core.
- `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts` and `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts` around phase/task create handlers and resolved parent lookup.
- Any shared helpers for entity creation, parent relinking, and sequence assignment.

Implementation goals:
1. Ensure every create/update path that accepts `featureId` / `phaseId` / task parent refs resolves human refs to a real internal entity before persisting.
2. Make global `Pxxx` / `Txxx` allocation safe against duplicate assignment during rapid or parallel creates.
3. Add regression tests covering both adapters and the core data layer.
4. Repair the current inconsistent live data (`F010` ↔ `P037`) once the root cause is fixed.

Behaviors to preserve:
- human refs (`F00x`, `P00x`, `T00x`, shortId, composite ref, title where allowed) remain accepted.
- global sequence semantics introduced in earlier work remain intact.
- repair must remain harness-agnostic and live in core/shared layers where possible.

tasks.title: Fix planner integrity regression for parent linking and global sequence allocation
tasks.description:
Root-cause and fix the remaining planner integrity issues exposed while creating F010/P037.

Concrete failures to address:
- `feature_get F010` reports `0 phases` while `phase_get P037` shows a valid phase with 11 tasks.
- `phase_list F010` returns no phases even though `P037` was intended to belong to it.
- An earlier parallel create attempt assigned duplicate `T141` refs, proving global task numbering is not safe under concurrent writes.

Work items:
1. Audit all create/update paths for feature↔phase and phase↔task parent linking across core, Pi adapter, and MCP handlers.
2. Identify whether unresolved human refs can still be persisted or whether derived feature containment can drift from phase files.
3. Fix global sequence allocation so no duplicate `Pxxx` / `Txxx` refs can be emitted under parallel or rapid successive mutations.
4. Add regression tests for:
   - human ref resolution on writes (`Fxxx` / `Pxxx` / `Txxx`)
   - concurrent/parallel task creation uniqueness
   - repair of the exact `F010` / `P037` incident
5. Repair current planner data after the code fix and verify `feature_get F010`, `phase_list F010`, and `task_list P037` are all consistent.

Primary files likely involved:
- `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts`
- `packages/plan-core/src/schema.ts`
- `packages/plan-core/src/naming.ts` and related helpers
- `packages/pi-adapter/src/index.ts`
- `packages/plan-mcp/src/index.ts`

Acceptance:
- a phase created/updated with `featureId: "Fxxx"` always links correctly or fails explicitly
- no duplicate global `Pxxx` / `Txxx` refs can be produced by the supported mutation paths
- regression tests are green
- F010/P037 inconsistency is repaired in the live planner data

---
**Completion summary:**
Implemented the planner integrity fix and repaired the live inconsistent data.

Code changes:
- `packages/plan-core/src/plan-store.ts`
  - made global sequence allocation atomic via `updateProject()` instead of read-then-save on `project.json`
  - added canonicalization of persisted phase `featureId` values when they were stored as human refs like `F010`
  - made `loadFeatures()` and `loadAll()` rebuild feature→phase containment from phases in memory instead of trusting stale `feature.phaseIds`
  - added `repairPhaseFeatureRefs()` to the core repair flow
  - added a cross-process filesystem lock around atomic writes so project/phase writes are serialized across separate processes, not only within one process
- Added regression tests:
  - `packages/plan-core/test/integrity-regression.test.mjs`
  - `packages/pi-adapter/test/ref-validation.test.mjs` (extended)
  - `packages/plan-mcp/test/ref-validation.test.mjs` (extended)

Live data repair performed:
- ran `PlanStore.repair()` on the project planner
- repaired `P037.featureId` from the persisted human ref `F010` to the real feature UUID
- rebuilt `F010.phaseIds` so the feature now correctly contains `P037`

Validation:
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/core build`
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/mcp build`
- `pnpm --filter @agent-plan/pi-adapter build`
- `node --test packages/plan-core/test/integrity-regression.test.mjs`
- `node --test packages/pi-adapter/test/ref-validation.test.mjs`
- `node --test packages/plan-mcp/test/ref-validation.test.mjs`
- `pnpm check`

State verified after repair:
- `feature_get F010` → now shows `1 phases`
- `phase_list F010` → now shows `P037(F010)`
- `phase_get P037` → now resolves under `F010`

Residual note:
- the repository still has unrelated uncommitted changes from the earlier planner-only governance migration and pre-existing web-ui/package edits; this task changed the core integrity path and test coverage, then repaired planner data.
